title: Chapter 5 — AI Quiz: Processor Fundamentals
instructions: Original AI-authored practice, not an official Cambridge or teacher paper. Answer all questions; written responses are self-marked using the guidance after submission. You can retake the quiz.
description: Original chapter practice: multiple-choice and written questions with self-marking guidance.

questions.text: Which register holds the address of the next instruction?
Which bus carries the address of a memory location?
State the purpose of the memory address register (MAR).

answer.text: Holds the address of the memory location currently being accessed.

questions.text: Describe two steps of the fetch stage.

answer.text: The address in the program counter is copied to the MAR.
The instruction is fetched from memory into the MDR and then copied to the CIR.

questions.text: Explain what an interrupt is and give one example.

answer.text: A signal that requests the processor’s attention, interrupting normal execution.
Example: input/output completion, timer or hardware fault.

questions.text: Describe one difference between an opcode and an operand.

answer.text: An operand supplies the data or address on which the operation acts.
